Issued at 300 AM EDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Currently-Tonight... KMLB radar imagery shows dry weather across 
east central Florida. GOES-16 satellite imagery and local 
observations indicate mostly clear to partly cloudy skies. 
Temperatures are currently in the mid 70s to low 80s with dew points 
in the mid 70s to around 80F degrees. Analysis charts show high 
pressure (~1022mb) over the eastern Gulf. Additionally, there's a 
500mb high over eastern Gulf and state of Florida with 500mb heights 
at 595dm (90th percentile), as well as a mid/upper level trough over 
the western Atlantic. 

Drier air in the mid to upper levels are expected to keep rain 
chances below normal today mostly due to a Saharan Dust Layer. 
Isolated to widely scattered showers (20-30% chance) and lightning 
storms are forecast to develop this afternoon and evening as 
collisions occur between sea breezes and outflow from previous 
showers/lightning storm. Rain chances diminish by around 8PM. Hi-res 
guidance shows MLCAPE up to 2,000-4,200 J/kg, 0-6km shear up to 10-
30kts, PWATs up to 1.80-2.30", and conditionally unstable mid-level 
lapse rates. Therefore, the potential exists for an isolated strong 
lightning storm or two capable of frequent lightning, wind gusts up 
to 30-50mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 1-3"). Afternoon highs in the 
low to mid 90s are forecast. A Heat Advisory has been issued for all 
of east central Florida from 11AM to 8PM for heat index values up to 
108-110F degrees. Remember to take frequent breaks from the heat, 
drink plenty of fluids, wear light colored clothing, and shift 
outdoor work away from the hottest parts of the day between the 
hours of 11am to 4pm. Near to above normal lows in low 70s to near 
80F degrees are forecast overnight.

Wednesday-Friday... Expect a similar forecast on Wednesday and 
Thursday with drier air in the mid to upper levels which will keep 
rain chances below normal. The aforementioned 500mb ridge is 
expected to shift west as the mid/upper level trough over the 
western Atlantic deepens on Wednesday into Thursday before the 
ridge builds over Deep South, as well as the state of Florida 
late week. 500mb heights are forecast to increase from 594dm 
(90th percentile) on Wednesday to 597dm (maximum percentile for 
this time of year) by Friday over the Deep South. This will result
in a slight increase in winds from the west at 5-10mph on 
Wednesday and Thursday before winds turn onshore with the east 
coast sea breeze over the coastal counties into the afternoon and 
evening each day. Isolated to scattered showers (20-30% chance on 
Wednesday and 20-40% chance Thursday/Friday) and lightning storms 
are forecast to develop into the afternoon and evening as 
collisions occur between sea breezes and outflow from previous 
showers/lightning storms. Guidance indicates high instability, 
weak to moderate bulk shear, PWATs up to 1.80- 2.3", as well as 
conditionally to absolutely unstable mid level lapse rates. Thus, 
the potential exists for isolated strong storms capable of 
producing frequent lightning, wind gusts up to 30-50mph, and heavy
rainfall (up to 1-3"). Afternoon highs in the low to mid 90s are 
forecast each day with near Heat Advisory criteria maximum heat 
index values up to 105F-110F degrees forecast. Lows in the low to 
upper 70s are forecast. 

Saturday-Monday... The heat wave is expected to continue through 
the forecast period as a longwave ridge builds over the eastern 
CONUS. Ensembles are in good agreement that 500mb heights will 
reach 597dm over the southeastern US before weakening (594dm) and 
gradually shifting slightly west-southwest on Monday. At the 
surface, high pressure is forecast to build over the eastern Gulf 
and Deep South. Light and variable winds are forecast to increase 
into the afternoon and evening on Saturday and Sunday at 5-10mph 
with the east coast sea breeze mainly along and south of I-4. 
Mostly dry to below normal rain chances are forecast over the 
weekend through Monday. High temperatures in the low to mid 90s 
with lows in the low to upper 70s. At least a Moderate to Major 
HeatRisk is forecast each day with a 20-40% chance of an Extreme 
HeatRisk for Lake county. A Major and Extreme HeatRisk affect 
anyone without adequate cooling and hydration.
